page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.3xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance belonging to the enhanced c7t family. Built on KVM hypervisor architecture, it features an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 6 physical cores offering 12 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. System memory is provisioned at 24 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The cache structure consists of 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2.

The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation and lacks local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk operations. Benchmark evaluation places the unit within the average performance bracket for stress-ng single-core (1867.59) and multi-core (11659.32) processing, Geekbench single-core (1530) and multi-core (7429) scores, and PassMark database operations (5747.67). Static web serving throughput reaches 16.68 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations achieve 11.93 million operations per second.

A hardware tradeoff is evident in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth (256MB), which measured 36.2 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom performance quartile. Similarly, medium-model (7B parameter) LLM prompt processing performance is lower at 24.2 tokens/sec. The higher core density relative to system memory offers cost efficiency for compute-focused workloads that do not require high memory footprints per vCPU. This configuration is suitable for software compilation, CI/CD processing, web serving, and general batch execution tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.3xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyperthreading, alongside 48 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning totals 24 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio tailored for CPU-bound processes. The instance lacks local storage, relying on remote block storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. Hardware support extends to AVX-512 VNNI vector processing and VAES cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results show average multi-core and single-core compute performance across standard tests, alongside 11.93 million Redis SET operations per second and 16.68 GB/sec static web serving throughput. A throughput limitation appears in uncached large-block memory reads (36.2 GB/sec), placing it in the lower benchmark tier for heavy sequential memory transfers. Target workloads include CI/CD build environments, software compilation, web serving, and general batch execution.
